description: Machine-readable baseline-decision audit for the first untouched continuous full-history SingleAnchor baseline. The PR #14 audit inventoried every baseline-relevant value, bound the approved data identity and exposed eight unresolved class-D decisions. All eight are now resolved by the approved baseline decisions recorded here and frozen in config/baseline-contract.json, which is the canonical source of the run's effective values. This register remains the decision record: for each field it records the class, the value and the source, and for the former blockers the authority, the approved decision and the preserved audit-time fixture/example context. The human-auditable decision record is ../BASELINE_CONFIGURATION_FREEZE_AUDIT.md, the human-auditable frozen contract is ../BASELINE_CONTRACT.md, and the executable Windows-local consistency checks are ../tests/SingleAnchor/BaselineDecisionAuditTests.cs and ../tests/SingleAnchor/BaselineContractTests.cs.

classification.A: explicitly approved/frozen by the authoritative project contract
classification.B: explicitly defined strategy default that is valid for the authoritative baseline
classification.C: fixture/test/example value only; recorded in fixtureValues, never a baseline value
classification.D: configurable value (or run policy) with no approved baseline value; no field carries class D any more, and a value can only return to class D by a deliberate re-opening of the decision

fields.source: approved baseline decision (2026-09-27), frozen in config/baseline-contract.json and recorded in BASELINE_CONFIGURATION_FREEZE_AUDIT.md section 10
fields.authority: the approved baseline decision: -AllowMissingData is enabled, but every failed request must be classified against the frozen contract, the run's persisted -RunEvidence invocation and the qualified continuous tree by scripts/Test-SingleAnchorBaselineFailedData.ps1; the classifier refuses a contract not pinned by the register, a run whose resolved invocation differs from the contract, a tree that no longer matches its composition manifest, and any run ending other than normal completion or AccountStopOut. -AllowEngineErrors remains prohibited.
fields.policy: enabled with mandatory classification: expected source-absent calendar days inside the frozen window, the enumerated known auxiliary benchmark path, and source-absent days after the actually processed horizon of an AccountStopOut run (the intended modeled terminal survival outcome) may be accepted; a failed request for a partition carrying qualified rows, an out-of-window or unknown request, a source-absent day within the processed horizon that was not requested at all, or a failed-request accounting mismatch between the engine data-monitor count and the failed-request lines invalidates the baseline
fields.whyRequired: Under the always-open XAUUSD/dukascopy/Cfd identity LEAN requests a partition for every calendar day. The qualified continuous record counts 406 source-absent calendar days plus 1 unrelated missing benchmark file (cfd/dukascopy/hour/xauusd.zip) as failed data requests. Without -AllowMissingData the helper turns those into exit code 3, so the authoritative procedure must define how those already-classified, expected failures are handled. It must not hide a failed request for a partition that carries rows, and it must not weaken the missing-data guard.
fields.currentCodeDefault: run-backtest.ps1 fails with exit code 3 when any local data request fails; -AllowMissingData downgrades that to a warning. The PR 1 qualification driver ran the probe with -AllowMissingData and classified every failed request in the qualification record.
fixtureExampleValues: -AllowMissingData in the tools README quick-start and qualification route
helper exit code 3 without it for the same data folder
fields.notAuthoritativeBecause: At the time of the PR #14 audit the qualification driver's flag belonged to the qualification run and no project document stated the strategy baseline's policy; the helper default would have made the authoritative run end as a failed helper exit rather than a documented expected outcome. The approved baseline decision was made separately from the qualification run.
fields.approvedDecision: Run with -AllowMissingData and classify every failed request (option a). -AllowEngineErrors must not be used. The strong distinction between expected source-absent requests, known non-strategy/auxiliary requests, unexpected missing qualified data and engine/runtime errors is preserved.
